# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 19)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of the first year
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; threatening rain (persistent but held off); frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett ("Old Ilrine"), herbalist born at Quenwick; Eldette Corrett, cooper born at Gulton

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- **Admiration for Caleb Garth**: Developed strong admiration for his work knowledge; Caleb greatly admires her
- **Business Philosophy**: Hopes to improve great piece of land and build many good cottages
- **Final Grange Encounter with Will**: Will declared passionately that best is over with him; stated what he cares for most is absolutely forbidden to him by his own pride and honor; acknowledged he would never woo her; spoke plainly that he would live like one who had seen heaven in a trance
- **Misinterpretation**: Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced sickening certainty that Will meant his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- **Internal Resolution**: Though thought throbbed through her that she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; memory of their limited time together seemed pale before memory of Will's constant companionship with someone else; credited all to simple friendship and cruel obstruction from husband's injurious act; adopted fortifying thought and wrote memoranda with ease
- **Departure from Grange**: Seated in carriage with bright eyes and blooming cheeks; threw back heavy "weepers"; caught sight of Will with portfolio under his arm on road; passed him as he raised his hat; felt pang at being seated in exaltation while leaving him behind; could not look back; felt crowd of indifferent objects thrust them asunder
- **Lingering Longing**: Wished she had known before and he had known, then they could be happy thinking of each other though forever parted; wished she could have given him money and made things easier; yet worldly weight bore heavily despite her independent energy; asked herself how he could dream of her defying husband's barrier, or she could defy it
- **About Casaubon's Codicil**: Forced to keep money that ought to have been his under Casaubon's codicil, causing her distress

**Will Ladislaw**
- **Grange Declaration**: Spoke impetuously about what he cares for most being forbidden him not merely by being out of reach but by his own pride and honor; stated he must know best is over while young; felt contradicting himself and offending self-approval but said not wooing a woman to tell her he would never woo her; acknowledged ghostly kind of wooing
- **Emotional State at Grange**: Consciousness overflowed by something suppressing utterance upon seeing her; both felt parting was near; stormy fluctuation of feelings; her words seemed cruelly neutral; looked pale and miserable; passionate love for her which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- **After Parting**: As carriage grew smaller, his certainty had much more bitterness; sight of Dorothea driving past while he felt himself plodding along as poor devil seeking position made conduct seem mere matter of necessity; had no assurance she loved him; could not pretend glad in having suffering on his own side
- **Remaining at Middlemarch**: Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting from Dorothea; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond Lydgate
- **Scandal**: Mrs. Cadwallader reports scandal spreading: Will making "sad dark-blue scandal by warbling continually" with Lydgate's wife; rumor claims constantly at their house
- **Raffles' Secret**: Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this, treating as card to play
- **Previous Family Revelations**: Raffles disclosed Will's father was at Boulogne, very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line—high style of receiving-house"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- **Bulstrode's Offer (Rejected)**: Bulstrode offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life, proportional capital at death, or more if necessary; **Will rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth are important; recognized stain he cannot help through his mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; states it ought to lie with a man's self that he is a gentleman; departed with determined quickness**
- **Morning After Rejection**: Wrote brief letter to Dorothea saying various causes detained him longer than expected; asked permission to call at Lowick at her mentioned hour, being anxious to depart but unwilling until granted interview

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court
- Peculiar man lacking curiosity about personal affairs; very fond of music; when he could afford it went to hear oratorios
- **Working with Railroads**: Had business at Yoddrell's farm to measure and value outlying piece of land belonging to Lowick Manor; bias towards getting best possible terms from railroad companies; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents; explained railroad cannot be hindered; warned interference would result in legal consequences
- **Commitment to Fred Vincy**: Committed to helping Fred forward; decided to take Fred on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Character**: Ruled absolutely only on other people's behalf; on ninety-nine points Mrs. Garth decided, but on hundredth point Caleb was immovable ruler

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother; intelligent, composed
- **Definitive Statement on Fred**: Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else...I should never be quite happy if I thought he was unhappy for the loss of me"; cannot imagine Fred preaching without it seeming a caricature
- **Reaction to Fred's News**: Upon Fred telling her of his engagement with her father, touched keenly; said hurriedly "I am so glad"; told Fred he was "too deliciously ridiculous" and "charming simpleton"; scolded him for not seeing Mr. Farebrother's delicate feeling
- **Internal Conflict and Resolution**: Saw possibility of new interpretations; felt she seemed to be slighting Mr. Farebrother; earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy; believes tender affection stored through years cannot be exchanged without cheapening one's life
- **Present Activity**: Telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage; tells Rumpelstiltskin tale with precision and repeat the same words exactly

**Fred Vincy**
- Son of Mr. Vincy; age four-and-twenty
- **Current Situation**: Rejected Church vocation; has taken his degree; encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm and helped enthusiastically with land measurement work
- **Caleb's Offer Accepted**: Caleb agreed to take him on as assistant; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- **Disclosure to Father**: Spoke formally and seriously; expressed regret for disappointing his father; Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; stated he will keep no horse for Fred and Fred must pay his own tailor
- **Evening Visit to Lowick**: Visited Lowick Rectory where Mary was copying labels; told Mary of his engagement with her father
- **Casual Mention of Ladislaw News**: Days later, casually mentioned to Rosamond what he had heard at Lowick Parsonage about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- **Acknowledged Debt**: Has acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged, even when able to pay it in money
- **Present Activity**: Seated near Mary at Lowick Parsonage during storytelling; watching her effectiveness with admiration

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician in Middlemarch; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture; pressure of sordid cares tightened considerably by merry Christmas bringing happy New Year, when fellow-citizens expect payment for goods bestowed on neighbors
- **Creditor Negotiations**: Offered bill of sale on furniture to Mr. Dover (silversmith and jeweller); Mr. Dover consented to take on upholsterer's credit also, accepting interest for a given term; bought purple amethysts costing thirty pounds as bridal present for Rosamond; Mr. Dover will reduce debt by taking back portion of plate and amethysts
- **Conversation with Rosamond about Debt**: Had been preparing to discuss debt with Rosamond; waited till evening with candles lit for quiet moment; spoke kindly; described debt and necessity for her help; she would not turn eyes on paper; quietly went out of room; gave his kiss; she returned it faintly; appearance of accord recovered temporarily; Lydgate flushed to roots of hair; felt helpless and wondering; seemed Rosamond had not identified herself with him as if creatures of different species
- **Financial Reality**: Year's bills coming in from tradesmen; Dover's threatening hold on furniture; nothing to depend on but slow dribbling payments from patients who must not be offended; handsome fees from Freshitt Hall and Lowick Manor easily absorbed; needs nothing less than thousand pounds to be freed from actual embarrassment; with Christmas season, pressure intensified
- **Emotional and Mental State**: Native warm-heartedness takes great deal of quenching; feels keenly manliness requires husband to feel that inexperienced girl got into trouble by marrying him; realizes Rosamond does not reverence his mind as he imagined; she is attracted to talent because it gives prestige, not from intellectual appreciation; memory of Dorothea's voice—that voice of deep-souled womanhood—had remained within him as enkindling conceptions; tones were music from which he was falling away; **now prey to worst irritation which arises not simply from annoyances, but from second consciousness underlying those annoyances, of wasted energy and degrading preoccupation, which was reverse of all his former purposes; bitter incessant murmur within him: "This is what I am thinking of; and that is what I might have been thinking of"; every difficulty becomes double goad to impatience**
- **Nature of His Discontent**: Discontent is not sense of stupendous self and insignificant world (which has consolations); rather it is sense that grand existence in thought and effective action lies around him, while his self is being narrowed into miserable isolation of egoistic fears and vulgar anxieties; troubles appear sordid and beneath attention of lofty persons; his discontent is hardest to bear because he sees what he might have been
- **Knowledge of Will-Dorothea Situation**: Knows a great deal more than he tells; imagines passionate attachment on both sides; understood the vacillation keeping Will at Middlemarch; **did not quite trust Rosamond's reticence towards Will, and he was right**
- **Hospital Work**: Giving great deal of time to New Hospital; Lydgate indefatigable; preparing new ward in case cholera comes to Middlemarch
- **Encounter with Farebrother**: Mr. Farebrother, having learned something making him watch eagerly for opportunity, met Lydgate at Lowick Parsonage drawing-room; Farebrother knew Lydgate was proud man but having little corresponding fibre in himself, hardly allowed enough for way Lydgate shrank from utterance of word about his private affairs; stepped out of whist-table to speak with him
- **Farebrother's Offer of Help**: Farebrother disclosed that Lydgate had privately done him service by helping him stop playing for money; credited Dorothea (Mrs. Casaubon) with this influence; offered friendly ear if Lydgate wanted to open himself about any difficulty; spoke of how right-doing depends on not being in want of money; expressed he no longer needs to hang on smiles of chance
- **Lydgate's Response to Offer**: **Could not bear the offer of help; after having been gratified with sense he had privately done Vicar a service, suggestion that Vicar discerned his need of service in return made him shrink into unconquerable reticence; feared mention of his case would imply wanting specific things; at that moment suicide seemed easier; even if inclined to openness, knew Farebrother could not give immediate help needed**

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Believing Lydgate's marriage delightful; regards Rosamond as amiable, docile creature though rather uninteresting—pattern-card of finishing-school
- **Awareness of Lydgate's Situation**: Aware that Lydgate is proud man; having little corresponding fibre in himself regarding personal dignity (except dignity of not being mean or foolish), hardly allows enough for way Lydgate shrank from discussing private affairs
- **Learning of Lydgate's Need**: After conversation at Mr. Toller's, learned something which made him watch eagerly for opportunity to indirectly let Lydgate know friendly ear was ready
- **At Lowick Parsonage**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate; disclosed that Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; thanked him for that good turn; expressed preference for being under obligation; spoke of strong check to self-complacency in finding how much right-doing depends on not being in want of money
- **Present Activity**: Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale; dramatizes intense interest in tale to please children; had been playing whist to satisfy his mother, who regards occasional whist as protest against scandal and novelty of opinion

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; fond of horseback riding; victorious obstinacy which never wastes energy in impetuous resistance
- **Riding Incident and Accident**: Captain Lydgate offered Rosamond a gentle gray horse; went riding without telling husband; after Lydgate's prohibition, manipulated him by asking him to fasten her plaits; determined to go riding again without informing him; on riding excursion with Captain Lydgate, gentle gray took fright at crash of tree being felled at Halsell Wood; accident led finally to loss of her baby
- **Current State**: Regaining brilliant health; now possessing knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will (learned from Fred Vincy); encouraged Will's musical companionship
- **Response to Debt Disclosure**: When Lydgate proposed returning amethysts and other items, responded with thin utterance throwing "What can I do" into complete neutrality; fell like mortal chill on Lydgate's roused tenderness; quietly left room after saying she would not look
- **Secret Disobedience**: Had already secretly disobeyed him by asking her father to help them; her father ended decisively by saying, "I am more likely to want help myself"
- **Romantic Speculation**: In her ennui and dissatisfaction, speculates romantically about Casaubon being jealous and laying plan to spoil marriage between Will and Dorothea

**Mrs. Vincy**
- Mother of Rosamond; seated at Lowick Parsonage with old lady (Mrs. Farebrother); cheerful disposition
- **About Rosamond**: Describes her daughter as having had "angel of a temper" from babyhood; never showed temper; was always good; has complexion beyond anything; notes Rosamond used to living in cheerful house with things going on; now married to husband out at odd hours, close and proud disposition (lowers tone indiscreetly)
- **About Her Children**: Has three little girls aged seven to eleven; claims all her children are good-tempered, thank God; Louisa is her darling

**Other Characters at Lowick Parsonage**: Three little girls (including Louisa, aged seven to eleven) listening to Mary's stories; Mr. Chichely; Mrs. Farebrother (old lady); Miss Farebrother

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Major Development**: Approximately fifteen months after Peter Featherstone's death, became proprietor of Stone Court through Joshua Rigg's land sale
- **Raffles' Appearances**: Met Mr. Raffles unexpectedly at Stone Court; Raffles recognized Bulstrode after twenty-five years; offered him quarterly annuity payments; Raffles demanded two hundred pounds to leave immediately, refused regular annuity, departed by three o'clock coach; later red-faced man with large whiskers appeared at house wanting to wait; Raffles appeared at Bank claiming he turned out of way to come to Middlemarch just to look about; wanted cool five-and-twenty pounds to go away; suggested he might come back for longer stay; declared would come back to Middlemarch before long
- **Bulstrode's Terror**: Feels helpless; certain that Raffles—unless providence sent death—would come back; terror of having disclosed to judgment of neighbors facts of past life which would render him object of scorn and opprobrium; terror of being judged sharpens memory; past becomes not dead history but still quivering part of himself; night and day without interruption save brief sleep felt scenes of earlier life coming between him and everything else
- **Past Life - Early Years**: Young banker's clerk with agreeable person; eminent though young member of Calvinistic dissenting church at Highbury; striking experience in conviction of sin and sense of pardon; called as Brother Bulstrode in prayer meetings; thought of ministry as possibly his vocation; **that was the happiest time of his life, the spot he would have chosen now to awake in and find the rest a dream**
- **Dunkirk Connection**: Orphan educated at commercial charity-school; invited to fine villa belonging to Mr. Dunkirk, richest man in congregation; became intimate there; setting-in of new current for his ambition
- **Pawnbroker Partnership**: Became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business—magnificent sort both in extent and profits; became aware one source of magnificent profit was easy reception of any goods offered without strict inquiry as to where they came from
- **Moral Compromise**: Remembered first moments of shrinking, filled with private arguments taking form of prayer; justified business through theological reasoning; peculiar spiritual experiences made retention of position seem service demanded of him; vista of fortune had already opened itself; found himself carrying on two distinct lives
- **Perpetual Self-Justification**: Years had been perpetually spinning pleas into intricate thickness like masses of spider-web, padding the moral sensibility; soul had become more saturated with belief that he did everything for God's sake, being indifferent to it for his own; yet if he could be back in that far-off spot with his youthful poverty, he would choose to be a missionary
- **Later Years**: Had mental exercises, called himself nought, laid hold on redemption; after five years Death came again, taking away his wife; he did gradually withdraw his capital but did not make sacrifices requisite to put end to business, which was carried on for thirteen years afterwards before it finally collapsed; Nicholas Bulstrode used his hundred thousand discreetly and became provincially, solidly important—banker, Churchman, public benefactor
- **Current Crisis**: When this respectability had lasted undisturbed for nearly thirty years—that past had risen and immersed his thought as if with terrible irruption of a new sense overburthening the feeble being
- **Nature of His Hypocrisy**: Not a coarse hypocrite who consciously affects beliefs for gulling the world; simply a man whose desires had been stronger than his theoretic beliefs, and who had gradually explained gratification of his desires into satisfactory agreement with those beliefs; if this be hypocrisy, it is process which shows itself occasionally in us all
- **Repentance and Restitution**: Had long poured out utterances of repentance; today a repentance came of bitterer flavor; threatening Providence urged him to kind of propitiation which was not simply doctrinal transaction; must bring restitution in his hand; divine tribunal had changed its aspect for him; self-prostration no longer enough
- **Offer to Will and Reaction**: Wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; paused after initial disclosure; Will asked if Bulstrode had not been connected with pawnbroker's business at west end where stolen goods had been received; Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain of his ground; could not tell a lie; answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; **offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at his death, or more if necessary; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept like a woman—first time he had encountered open expression of scorn from any man higher than Raffles; with that scorn hurrying like venom through his system, there was no sensibility left to consolations; had to check weeping when wife and daughters came home from hearing address of Oriental missionary**

**Mr. Raffles**
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claims to be visiting his stepson Joshua Rigg
- **Critical Discovery and Secret**: Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; **deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode**—holds secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as a card to play
